author: BStoimenov <B.L.Stoimenov@gmail.com>
message:
Enable loading of 32-bit float WAV files by switching from pydub to scipy.io.wavread

This edit enable loading of 32-bit float WAV files by switching from
pydub to scipy.io.wavread

It is related to issue #328.
The existing function `read_audio_generic` relies on
`pydyb.AudioSegment` to load the data, but has a few problems:
1. Assumes that data is int16 or int32,
2. There no obvious (at least to me) way to query if the underlying
wav-file data is actually 32-bit float
3. Relies on deprecated `numpy.fromstring` conversion, which should be
replaced by `numpy.frombuffer`

For ".wav" files, the problem is solved by using `scipy.io.wavread` in
`read_audio_file`, instead of calling `read_audio_generic` and `pydyb`.
For ".au" files, the problem of loading 32-bit float audio remains, but
they are relatively rarely used.
As for the ".mp3" and ".ogg" files, they are non-PCM, lossy compression
formats, and do not have associated bit depths[*], so no change is
needed.

[*] Bit depth is only meaningful in reference to a PCM digital signal.
Ogg Vorbis Decoder has the option to set the output to a floating
number, which is not the same thing as bit depth of PCM-encoded data.

author: Christian Clauss <cclauss@me.com>
message:
GitHub Action to lint Python code

Output: https://github.com/cclauss/pyAudioAnalysis/actions

https://flake8.pycqa.org/en/latest/user/error-codes.html

On the flake8 test selection, this PR does _not_ focus on "_style violations_" (the majority of flake8 error codes that [__psf/black__](https://github.com/psf/black) can autocorrect).  Instead, these tests are focus on runtime safety and correctness:
* E9 tests are about Python syntax errors usually raised because flake8 can not build an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).  Often these issues are a sign of unused code or code that has not been ported to Python 3.  These would be compile-time errors in a compiled language but in a dynamic language like Python, they result in the script halting/crashing on the user.
* F63 tests are usually about the confusion between identity and equality in Python.  Use ==/!= to compare str, bytes, and int literals is the classic case.  These are areas where __a == b__ is True but __a is b__ is False (or vice versa).  Python >= 3.8 will raise SyntaxWarnings on these instances.
* F7 tests logic errors and syntax errors in type hints
* F82 tests are almost always _undefined names_ which are usually a sign of a typo, missing imports, or code that has not been ported to Python 3.  These also would be compile-time errors in a compiled language but in Python, a __NameError__ is raised which will halt/crash the script on the user.

author: Matt Rendina <rendinam@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Explicitly request use of conda in Jenkinsfile

This change causes the creation of a new conda environment used to host the build as per the `conda_packages` docs here: https://github.com/spacetelescope/jenkins_shared_ci_utils/blob/master/README.md and removes the `with_env` commands which are then no longer necessary.

The error noted in issue #403 was caused by the Jenkinsfile not requesting the use of conda (by populating the `conda_packages` list for a given build configuration). A leftover pre-installed conda in the job's container was used by default, which allowed the `conda` commands specified in the build configuration to execute, though on a conda base environment, rather than a new target environment, which is not desired.

As an additional safeguard, future build containers on the Jenkins host will do away with the built-in conda installation to make the behavior more consistent.

message:
Sqlite db backend for TrajInfo (len, dim, offsets) (#798)

* [coordinates/TrajectoryInfoCache] implemented sqlite backend

Sqlite provides database locking for parallel filesystems, so we can use it on
clusters to cache trajectory information.

A LRU pattern has been implemented to clean least recently used entries.
The entries are spread over several databases to avoid locking timeouts.

The hash function is now computed via python stdlib hashlib and uses MD5.

Large overhaul of the final section in the "Work Chain" module, which shows
how to submit calculation jobs inside a work chain.

Switches to using the `AddWorkChain` as a starting point for adding the
calculation job, now that the added multiply step is added in an exercise.

using the calculation job in the `MultiplyAddWorkChain` as an exercise.

author: Sebastiaan Huber <mail@sphuber.net>
message:
Dependencies: update `Sphinx` and `jinja2` for compability

Jinja2 recently removed some resources that were still being used by
Sphinx 3. Upgrading both solves the issue. `myst-nb` also needed to be
upgraded to get compatibility with the newer version of `Sphinx`.

For the newer version of `myst-nb` the `nb_render_priority` variable is
no longer necessary and so is removed. The `jupyter_execute_notebooks`
variable was renamed to `nb_execution_mode`. Finally, the
`substitutions` keyword are now namespaced under `myst`.

message:
Added the the band-structure notebook ()

   (Copy of the commit message from aiida_demos)
   Finished the conversion to aiida 1.0b3, and the latest quantum-espresso plugin.
   The workchain now runs correctly with the SSSP v1.1, efficiency.
   Tests by me and @borellim.

   Minor issue: for one example (GaAs) the default time and computing power
   is not enough to finish the job, so the obtained band structure is
   incomplete (path L-W-X is empty).
   That is the longest example we provide (it takes almost 2h on my workstation)
   An increase of the default from 1800s to 3600s solves the problem for me.
   This could be implemented in 3 possible ways that I see:
   - default be modified in the QE plugin
   - parameters to be provided as an option in the submission, at the price of a more complicated
   input for the user of the notebook, but with the advantage of showing that modification
   to the turn-key solution are allowed.

   results_GaAs = launch.run(
       PwBandStructureWorkChain,
       code=code,
       structure=structure_GaAs,
       scf_options = Dict(dict={
           'resources': {
               'num_machines': 1
           },
           'max_wallclock_seconds' : 3600
       })
   )

   - provide a modification of the protocol with reduced accuracy ('fast' keyword)
   for this specific case (might still not be enough time, depending on the VM type).
   This also complicates the input, but provided additional info about the plugin

author: Julian Geiger <julian.geiger@psi.ch>
message:
📝 DOCS: Updates for compatibility with AiiDA v2.5.1

These minor changes fix issues and deprecation warnings that arose when going through the tutorial with the latest AiiDA v2.5.1. The modifications are mainly:
- Update the `verdi code setup` to `verdi code create` commands
- Update the SSSP version from 1.1 to 1.3 to reflect the change of default in `aiida-pseudo`
- Prepend `core` in the `DataFactory` calls where applicable, as well as `query.queryhelp` -> `query.as_dict()` in the `querying` notebook

One could also update the outputs, for instance, to reflect the change from `Info` to `Report` for the `verdi process` commands, as well as adding the additional information on caching which is now shown to avoid confusion, though it's not really necessary for being able to work through the material.

I understand that this page was initially intended for the AiiDA courses, so it's good to have a frozen version for each edition of the course. Though, as we'd like to eventually integrate this material into the main documentation (see issue #XXXX), I think it's good to have it updated now.

Lastly, a few deprecation warnings remain, for example:
```shell
- aiida/cmdline/groups/dynamic.py:145: AiidaDeprecationWarning: Relying on `_get_cli_options` is deprecated. The options should be defined through a `pydantic.BaseModel` that should be assigned to the `Config` class attribute. (this will be removed in v3)
- aiida/orm/nodes/data/code/legacy.py:42: AiidaDeprecationWarning: The `Code` class is deprecated. To create an instance, use the `aiida.orm.nodes.data.code.installed.InstalledCode` or `aiida.orm.nodes.data.code.portable.PortableCode` for a "remote" or "local" code, respectively. If you are using this class to compare type, e.g. in `isinstance`, use `aiida.orm.nodes.data.code.abstract.AbstractCode`. (this will be removed in v3)
- aiida/orm/nodes/data/code/legacy.py:172: AiidaDeprecationWarning: `Code.get_description` method is deprecated, use the `description` property instead. (this will be removed in v3)
```
however, I think these have to be adressed in the `src`.

author: Sebastiaan Huber <mail@sphuber.net>
message:
Add a download link for `perovskites` export archive

The query builder part of the tutorial depends on some data being
present in the database. This data would be imported for the virtual
machine so it would be available to users during the tutorial. Importing
the archive was not enough, as it relied on some extras being set, which
at the time were not exportable. Therefore a script had to be run after
importing that would set these extras and recreated the groups for the
pseudo potential families. The archive was not made available publicly
which means that users running the tutorial in their own environment and
database could not perform this last section.

These problems have now been addressed:

 * The archive was migrated from v0.3 to v0.4 with `aiida-core==1.0.0b3`
 * The migrated archive was imported into a clean database
 * The pseudo potential family groups were recreated
 * The extras were set on the calculations and structure nodes:
   - Structure formula was set on the calculation node
   - `A` and `B` element of `ABO3` perovskite formule set on structure
 * The 3 pseudo family groups and 3 calculation groups were exported.
   - Only direct inputs and outputs of the calculations were included

The text in the query builder notebook has been updated to include a
link to this archive. For now this is a dropbox link, but should be
replaced with a permanent link once the archive is fully tested and
confirmed to be correct.

hiding the code in a magic utility function.

author: Sebastiaan Huber <mail@sphuber.net>
message:
Add a download link for `perovskites` export archive (#35)

The query builder part of the tutorial depends on some data being
present in the database. This data would be imported for the virtual
machine so it would be available to users during the tutorial. Importing
the archive was not enough, as it relied on some extras being set, which
at the time were not exportable. Therefore a script had to be run after
importing that would set these extras and recreated the groups for the
pseudo potential families. The archive was not made available publicly
which means that users running the tutorial in their own environment and
database could not perform this last section.

These problems have now been addressed:

 * The archive was migrated from v0.3 to v0.4 with `aiida-core==1.0.0b3`
 * The migrated archive was imported into a clean database
 * The pseudo potential family groups were recreated
 * The extras were set on the calculations and structure nodes:
   - Structure formula was set on the calculation node
   - `A` and `B` element of `ABO3` perovskite formule set on structure
 * The 3 pseudo family groups and 3 calculation groups were exported.
   - Only direct inputs and outputs of the calculations were included

The text in the query builder notebook has been updated to include a
link to this archive. For now this is a dropbox link, but should be
replaced with a permanent link once the archive is fully tested and
confirmed to be correct.

author: Sebastiaan Huber <mail@sphuber.net>
message:
Fix the querybuilder notebook instructions of section 5 (#80)

* Fix the querybuilder notebook instructions of section 5

The instructions now tell the user to download the notebook, for which a
link is provided, and to save it to their machine. They can then launch
the jupyter server and open the notebook.

A section was added to the very first section to explain how these
download links can be used straight on a machine to which they are SSH
connected using `wget`. The text in section 5 has been adapted to this
to remove explicit mentioning of the virtual machine, in order to not
confuse those that are following it without our VM.

Note that I also removed the `.gitignore` in the `notebooks` folder. It
is true that there is a script to generate the two versions from the
template, however, this was necessary when they were still hosted in the
`aiida-demos` directory. For the tutorial VM this was then checked out
and as preparational step, the `scripts/make_notebook.py` was ran.
However, now these versions need to always be present in the repository
for them to be downloadable. They should occassionally just be
regenerated through the script if the content in the template changes.

* PR suggestions by @ltalirz

author: ramirezfranciscof <ramirezfranciscof@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
NEW: section on troubleshooting calculations

I took the content of the former `running computations` section that was
specific for troubleshooting errors and created a new module for it.

It includes:

1. An introduction with a warning of the previous knowledge required,
   together with a link to the section where to get it.

2. A setup subsection where they prepare the calculation; I propose to
   use the builder of pw and give them the faulty input parameters, but
   setting up the structure, kpoints and pseudo is left as exercise.

3. Dry run to simulate the submission.

4. Troubleshooting an error: check the process status, the logs, the
   output, and the inputs.

5. Restarting the calculation using `get_builder_restart`.

author: Sebastiaan Huber <mail@sphuber.net>
message:
Section 2 and 4: setup profile, computer and codes

This section will explain the concept of profiles by creating one
specifically for the tutorial through `verdi quicksetup`. This will also
make the tutorial usable for people that are not running through the
virtual machine but their own installation.

Additionally, section 4 will now give instructions on how to setup a
computer and a code. For people running on the virtual machine, prepared
yaml configuration files that can be used with the `--config` option are
provided. People running on their own installation will have to adapt
thse. Instructions to do so are added in an appendix which is currently
just a stub.
